title: ADR-015: What the owner says can add requirements and never remove one, and silence is not a "no"
ADR-016: The OWASP data files: one copy while both versions lived here, and two since
ADR-017: `sv` never writes the app's code
ADR-018: `sv` checks apps written in any language, with rules of its own among the checks
ADR-019: `sv` runs the app in a container on a network with no way out
ADR-020: `sv` is written in Rust
ADR-021: A crash's or a rate limiter's answer is never read as the app refusing
ADR-022: Whose word counts, and at which tier
ADR-023: False alarms and accepted risks a person records, and test code's findings listed apart
ADR-024: An unanswered data list holds the app to ASVS level 2
ADR-025: `sv run` has an end
ADR-026: The owner's word counts only when `sv review` recorded it
ADR-027: `sv probe` asks only public addresses, and only the ones it checked
ADR-028: Decide before you build: the design comes first, and nothing is credited for it
ADR-029: Exit codes: 2 only when a check could not run, 1 only when asked, 3 when `sv` failed
ADR-030: A plan before any code
ADR-031: A `not-the-app` list that would set apart all of the app's code is not used
ADR-032: Git, run in the app's folder, runs no program the app's repository names
ADR-033: CVSS v4 scores, computed with FIRST's own tables
ADR-034: A report is offered as `sv`'s only when its seal shows `sv` wrote it
ADR-035: A preflight of the run settings, read from the code and never run
ADR-036: `sv` finds its data beside itself, and an install does not live in a working folder
ADR-037: A Python project with no lockfile does not pin, `setup.py` and `setup.cfg` included
ADR-038: The SQL injection probe only reads, only on `sv`'s own copy of the app, and only ever finds
ADR-039: The sign-in token checks, and which key addresses they may name
ADR-040: A credential name over a sentence is reported low, and says so
ADR-041: One run at a time in a report folder, held by a lock file `sv` writes there
ADR-042: The test model answers in the shape the app asked for, and a wrong shape refused is credit for C7.1.1
ADR-043: A seal is a signature any computer can check, against keys the owner chose to trust
ADR-044: The coding prompts shown to work reach the AI tool when it builds what they are for
ADR-045: The app's own tools are called in a loop only when the owner marks them read-only
ADR-046: Compressed archives sent to the upload, to the limits the owner states
ADR-047: V3.4.3 is credited only for a Content-Security-Policy with the directives it names
ADR-048: The weak password-derivation rule cites storing passwords as well as making keys
ADR-049: `sv` reads the AI coding tool's own files in the project folder, apart from the app's grade
ADR-050: The app's own tests are a tier of their own, below an automated check
ADR-051: The tests must pass before a pull request merges into main, and every commit on main is tested
ADR-052: Packages installed before the run, outside the fence, in a container that sees only the dependency files
ADR-053: Another user's records are checked for reading, listing, changing, and deleting, and one read alone is "checked in part"
ADR-054: Templates and notebooks are read for what they can hold, and never pass silently
ADR-055: Two checks stop resting on one sample: cross-site access asks the private pages, and a common password is three
ADR-056: An error answer is credited only when the app was made to give one, and it was clean
ADR-057: A dashboard for `sv`, optional, with history kept only when the owner asks, outside the app's folder
ADR-058: A private set of pages for the owner to read `sv`'s documentation, in the home folder, without the paper
ADR-059: Every check that gives credit is seen withholding it in the test suite, or the build fails
ADR-060: One file per design entry
ADR-061: One file per backlog item, with a status line
ADR-062: The product is StackVet; the command stays `sv`
ADR-063: StackVet's logo is the code bracket, in terracotta
